title: What If the Sun Swelled Into a Red Giant?

scenes.text: What if the Sun swelled into a red giant? Earth would die long before it was swallowed.
The Sun brightens about one percent every 100 million years. In roughly a billion years, the oceans begin to boil.
Around five billion years from now, the Sun's core runs out of hydrogen and its outer layers start to swell.
It grows to about 250 times its current width, swallowing Mercury and probably Venus.
One leading model says tides and drag would pull Earth into the Sun's outer layers and shrink its orbit.
In that model, Earth vaporizes. Either way, the oceans have been gone for billions of years by then.
